`Most people with a healthy liver do not need a liver supplement` , and no product can "detox" or cleanse a liver that already filters waste on its own. Clinical evidence for liver supplements is mixed, and most studies focus on people with specific liver conditions—such as metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD, formerly NAFLD)—rather than general wellness.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAES0wEBxCJF1wsDRes8OSrUB6zKC5PZA6vaLvHfheDTve9srk6_gJK-Assj4cWnlYd1E5Ndq4Kzk8TJ6LHQvB-hA2T25Qi4vqj8eYxyZVkj6mWDbAASZtwSOO2N65qjfDFTG5hAFMAiFiXbR--Bt4ddQBlnpXDfpbqPMw7qYCVFkmi53uLmjvsWGblKafhsel0X5NvwCiU5VvS3sLDcIg933-YAPaZgoHQyVU09r_VFbFOEB0-2EeoOf75NCzjACM531T1p0DWBAQMQVngGzszPcEJ6-YZu)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1-qZ1KuATmLEF1d1Aevk168fMbgubFIz6bqeHu7PfvaoZohxwiCvwxbwnab0q1rNZ_bCVxOAl51UIQwAYkCUWsGdrGu1T2-gUuuDhWa5_pWgt8JNNe30lwmHqin_TmQ23Q7DriajuF3oXd5njW-CgxtWVGoSLMa5vWi-rlj_AuztQHUOVbXDgzIxToc)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbwHEIkXXs4WF_OoqDLhgni-w0yxi5iBvGQGqnFDMcW4y-DjRH5ELVkLqN_H62cK1HF3LtIi1kvAoyTfi_gwFa7EEdQEu1B4j6zVqY6s1g5FdxmhMKaCqgB-aE5Pyz6WXQFMk0U556y-gtBy7EVGNfg)

- **Milk thistle (silymarin):** Widely found in liver blends; some studies note modest reductions in liver enzyme markers, though clear clinical benefits for liver outcomes remain limited.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1-qZ1KuATmLEF1d1Aevk168fMbgubFIz6bqeHu7PfvaoZohxwiCvwxbwnab0q1rNZ_bCVxOAl51UIQwAYkCUWsGdrGu1T2-gUuuDhWa5_pWgt8JNNe30lwmHqin_TmQ23Q7DriajuF3oXd5njW-CgxtWVGoSLMa5vWi-rlj_AuztQHUOVbXDgzIxToc)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbwHEIkXXs4WF_OoqDLhgni-w0yxi5iBvGQGqnFDMcW4y-DjRH5ELVkLqN_H62cK1HF3LtIi1kvAoyTfi_gwFa7EEdQEu1B4j6zVqY6s1g5FdxmhMKaCqgB-aE5Pyz6WXQFMk0U556y-gtBy7EVGNfg)

items.title: Common Ingredients & What Research Shows
items.text: Milk thistle (silymarin): Widely found in liver blends; some studies note modest reductions in liver enzyme markers, though clear clinical benefits for liver outcomes remain limited. Artichoke leaf extract: Early trials suggest it may help lower liver enzymes in people with fatty liver disease, though larger human studies are still needed. Curcumin (turmeric): May help reduce liver inflammation and fat alongside lifestyle changes, but evidence is still developing. Omega-3 fatty acids: Fatty fish is the preferred source; supplements show mixed results for reducing liver fat or scarring. Vitamin E: Sometimes used under medical supervision for specific fatty liver cases, but high doses carry health risks and are not recommended for general liver support. N-Acetylcysteine (NAC): Used medically in hospitals for acetaminophen overdose; evidence is limited for everyday liver health in healthy individuals.
